correctness.rationale: A triangular cactus assembled by attaching two new vertices per triangular block has global torus coordinates (phi_i,psi_i) after quotienting the common phase. Its energy is exactly a sum of e=cos phi+cos psi+cos(phi-psi). Solving sine stationarity gives exactly two minima at -3/2 with Hessian index0, three saddles at -1 index1, and one maximum at 3 index2, all nondegenerate; block-diagonal Hessian inertia yields (2+3zt+z9t2)^r. Chirality change crosses sin(phi-psi)=0 and forces e>=-1 on some block; holding others at ground energy proves barrier >=E*+1/2. Explicit path (s,-s), s from 2pi/3 to 4pi/3, reaches max -1 and proves equality for all pairs via sequential flips. Standard Morse handles yield 2^r contractible components below first saddle, then connected wedge of 3r2^(r-1)-2^r+1 circles before +1; only 0 and 1 handles appear. Friendship block swaps force equal Haar basin masses 2^-r, and Hessian L(G)/2 gives spectral gap 1/2 (r>=2) or 3/2 (r=1). Full vertex flow need not decouple.
